subject: Re: Interested in Redwood — GitHub integration questions (Demo and pilot)
messages:
From: Sam Patel <sam@openlib.org>
To: camila_reyes@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Interested in Redwood — GitHub integration questions

Hey Camila,

We just signed up for Redwood via the self-serve flow after seeing the GitHub integration note in your docs. I lead integrations at OpenLib and we have a repo (https://github.com/openlib/openlib-integration) where we're experimenting with an embedded indexing + sync flow.

Before we schedule a demo I had a couple quick questions:
- Does Redwood support incremental sync from GitHub repos (only changes to files) or do we need a full re-index?
- Any recommended model/quantization profile for large codebases (millions of lines across many repos)?
- Is there a connector or reference implementation for the GitHub webhooks + Redwood ingest?

Happy to book a short demo if it's useful — we can include one of our engineers. Timezone: PST. Thanks!

— Sam
Sam Patel
Integrations Lead, OpenLib
sam@openlib.org
From: camila_reyes@redwood.ai
To: Sam Patel <sam@openlib.org>
Cc: alex_martinez@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 09:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Interested in Redwood — GitHub integration questions

Hi Sam —

Great to hear you signed up, and thanks for the repo link — that helps. Quick answers up front and then we can demo the workflow:

- Incremental sync: yes, Redwood supports incremental updates. We have a lightweight connector pattern that consumes GitHub webhooks and issues delta updates to the ingest pipeline so you don't need to re-index everything.
- Model/quantization: for large codebases we usually recommend a code-tuned open model (e.g., CodeX-ish family) with int8 quantization; our Optimize tool will propose batching/quant profiles based on token distributions. We can share concrete perf numbers for your repo shape during the call.
- Reference: we have an example connector in our docs and a sample implementation (Node + serverless) that we can share; I'll attach the spec and a one-pager.

Would you be available for a 30-min demo tomorrow (Wed) at 10:00 or 15:00 PST? If those don't work, send a couple of slots and we'll align. I'll loop in Alex (solutions engineer) to cover the connector details.

Attachments: redwood-one-pager.pdf, openlib-integration-spec.pdf

Best,
Camila Reyes
SDR, Redwood Inference
camila@redwood.ai

From: camila_reyes@redwood.ai

Cc: alex_martinez@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 10:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Interested in Redwood — GitHub integration questions

Perfect — 10:30 PST works. Alex, looping you in to cover the sharding/retry details.

Quick answers for the meeting:
- Max repo size per job: we don't enforce a hard limit, but practical throughput and memory considerations mean we often split large repos into reasonable shards (e.g., ~500k LOC chunks) for parallel ingest. We'll show the shard strategy in the demo.
- Webhook handling: our reference connector includes idempotency and exponential backoff for delivery failures; the hosted connector will surface retries in the dashboard. If you run the connector yourself, you can plug in your preferred queue/backoff implementation and Redwood will accept idempotent dedup keys.

Here is a calendly link to lock the 30-min slot: https://calendly.com/camila-reyes/30min — I booked provisional 10:30 and sent a calendar invite (you should see it shortly). If that doesn't arrive, let me know and I'll re-send.

Thanks — looking forward to the call.

Best,
Camila
